Luxembourg-France Income and Capital Tax Treaty (1958, as amended)
Luxembourg-United Kingdom Double Taxation Convention (1967, as amended by exchange of letters)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (AML/CFT Law), as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 30 August 2019 relating to the Register of Beneficial Owners; CSSF Regulation 12-02 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 23 December 1998 establishing a Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF), as amended.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the SCSp partnership agreement (contrat de société) for the proposed entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the entity's home jurisdiction or Luxembourg notary if notarised in Luxembourg

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / official excerpt from the foreign trade register for each corporate UBO (if any)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company register or trade registry of the UBO's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarised power of attorney appointing the Luxembourg incorporator or managing partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction of execution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarised and apostilled passport copies of all ultimate beneficial owners (natural persons)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent local authority or notary in the passport-holder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming identity and commercial standing of each UBO and the proposed SCSp's beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed financial institution, countersigned by notary if required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence for Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) as defined under Luxembourg AML/CFT Law and CSSF Regulation 12-02; mandatory screening against the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF) list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, EU restrictive measures, United Nations Security Council sanctions lists, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, and INTERPOL notices. Screening must cover all UBOs, managing partners, statutory auditors, and any person holding power of representation. A documented risk-based approach must be maintained, with independent audit trails, and any positive PEP or sanctions hit requires filing a suspicious transaction report (STR) with the CRF prior to incorporation if a related transaction is contemplated.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS Online portal (www.lbr.lu); official register: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official filing language for name reservation is French, but the proposed company name may be in any language using Latin characters. Names must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet for registration. The name must be distinctive, not contrary to public order or bonnes mœurs, and must not create a risk of confusion with existing registered names or international distinctive signs. The name of an SCSp may include the legal form 'SCSp' or 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' in full or abbreviated form. The law requires the name to be preceded or followed by the legal form indication, which must appear on all business documents.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCS rejects a name reservation application, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) within 15 days of the notification of rejection, requesting a reasoned reconsideration. The appeal must be submitted in French or German, accompanied by the original rejection notice, a corrected name proposal, and any supporting evidence of distinctiveness or lawful entitlement. If the LBR upholds the rejection, the applicant may file a further appeal with the Administrative Tribunal of Luxembourg within three months. Alternatively, the applicant may submit a new name reservation application with a revised name immediately, without prejudice to the administrative appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office arrangement is permissible for an SCSp only where a licensed Luxembourg domiciliation agent maintains the registered office, receives official correspondence, and keeps the required registers, minutes, and books at that address. The virtual office must not be used as a means to circumvent Luxembourg's substance requirements or to mislead third parties. For a wholesale distribution vehicle in ISIC 4669, the domiciliation agent must be able to demonstrate that the SCSp has adequate personnel, premises, and economic activity in Luxembourg if tax transparency or treaty benefits are sought.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 35% probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first 24 months of operations, due to the medium-to-high AML/CFT risk tier assigned to bulk petrochemical trading and the Luxembourg supervisory authority's focus on shell-like structures, particularly those relying on virtual offices or third-party domiciliation agents.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS court clerk registration and publication of the SCSp in the Luxembourg official gazette (Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations, RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing fee and RESA publication tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration filing with the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing fee for the RBE register

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Home-country competent ministry, foreign ministry, and Luxembourg consulate as applicable
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official consular and apostille fee schedule per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: First-year registered office and domiciliation fee with a licensed Luxembourg domiciliation agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a standard commercial SCSp domiciliation package

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Contingency reserve for unanticipated RCS clarification fees, courier of original apostilled documents, and administrative appeals (if any)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Reasonable contingency benchmark of 10% of total pre-incorporation costs

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, notably Part I and Articles 1 to 16 (SCSp regime introduced by the 2016 reform)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés - RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of constitution (acte constitutif) and the SCSp partnership agreement, registered with the RCS and published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés (RES)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum statutory capital for an SCSp; no escrow account is mandatory. Contributions may be in cash or in kind. General partners have unlimited liability; limited partners are liable only up to their agreed contribution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the initial capital of the Partnership be subscribed in accordance with the terms of the notarial deed of incorporation; that each General Partner's contribution is recorded in the Partnership's capital accounts; that the registered office of the Partnership be established at [address] in Luxembourg, with all statutory notices served there; that [Name] be and is hereby appointed Manager(s) with full power to act, jointly/individually, including authority to open bank accounts, appoint correspondents, negotiate and execute commercial agreements, and make requisite filings; that the managers are authorized to initiate the RCS registration and publication procedures; that any prior act performed on behalf of the Partnership before incorporation is ratified; and that this resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and execute the notarial deed of constitution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Luxembourg notary to prepare the SCSp partnership agreement and notarial deed. Verify the identities and capacities of all partners and the proposed manager. Execute the deed before the notary, either in person or by valid power of attorney, and obtain certified notarial copies.
required_dossiers: Passport or national identity card of each partner
Passport of each proposed manager
Power of attorney if a non-resident signatory is used
Draft partnership agreement containing profit-sharing, management and governance provisions
Proof of registered office address (lease agreement or written consent of the building owner)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises KYC or legal capacity queries, provide certified translations, apostilles or corporate extracts. Any drafting errors may be corrected and the deed re-executed without substantive delay at the notary’s discretion.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open a Luxembourg bank account and arrange any agreed capital contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution under CSSF supervision
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarial deed, KYC documentation and the proposed manager’s signatory authority to the bank. Deposit any agreed initial contribution or obtain a bank confirmation letter if required by commercial counterparties. No escrow account is legally required for an SCSp.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarial deed
Partner identification documents and proof of source of funds
Manager identification and banking signatory mandate
Fully completed bank account application form
Short business description covering wholesale petrochemical polymer trading
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced economic substance evidence, provide a business plan, projected trade volumes, and confirmation of the commercial purpose of the SCSp.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File registration with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the certified notarial deed and the required legal form with the RCS, specifying the company name, registered office, manager(s) and general partner details. Pay the prescribed registration fee and obtain the RCS registration number.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarial deed of constitution
Legal entity reference form (formulaire RCS)
Consent of the registered office address
Signed acceptance of appointment by each manager
Payment confirmation of the RCS registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or a case de carence, respond with corrected or supplementary information within 15 days. Missing exhibits may be filed separately as a déclaration complémentaire.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm publication in the electronic compendium of companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil électronique des sociétés (RES), facilitated by LBR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, verify that the RES publication contains the company name, form, registered office, partners, managers, and notarial deed date. Retrieve the RES excerpt and maintain a compliance copy in the corporate files.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate
RCS registration number
Extract of the notarial deed submitted for publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RES excerpt is incomplete, submit a written request to LBR to supplement the publication and obtain an amended extract.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Luxembourg tax and VAT registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SCSp for direct tax purposes to obtain the national business registration number (matricule). Assess VAT obligations and register for VAT if taxable supplies exceed the Luxembourg VAT threshold or cross-border supplies require a Luxembourg VAT number.
required_dossiers: RCS extract
Certified copy of the notarial deed
Particulars of partners and managers, including residences
Business activity description covering wholesale of polyethylene and polypropylene granules
VAT registration form where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authorities request economic substance information, provide the registered office lease, bank account confirmations and projected turnover statements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the declaration of beneficial owners with the RBE
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE) operated by Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Identify any natural person owning or controlling more than 25% of the SCSp, or who otherwise exercises control. Submit the RBE declaration online and obtain the acknowledgement of registration.
required_dossiers: Completed RBE declaration form
Ownership and control structure chart
Identification documents of each ultimate beneficial owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RBE declaration is inconsistent with RCS data, file a rectification through the RBE portal within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for social security as an employer (if hiring staff)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the SCSp intends to hire employees in Luxembourg, complete the employer registration with the CCSS within eight days of the first hire. Obtain the employer identification number for monthly salary declarations and social contributions.
required_dossiers: RCS extract
SCSp tax identification number (matricule)
Employment contract or draft for the first employee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed, file late with the CCSS and submit any outstanding social declarations; penalties may be mitigated upon showing good faith and prompt correction.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for pure wholesale distribution; if classified installation thresholds are crossed, the competent authority is the Administration de l'environnement under the policy oversight of the Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating license is required for non-manufacturing wholesale trading of polymer granules. A classified establishment registration may be necessary under the Luxembourg Law of 9 May 2014 on classified establishments (établissements classés) if warehousing or storage activities exceed applicable thresholds.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA: wholesale trading and storage of virgin polyethylene and polypropylene granules fall below hazardous substance thresholds; only an optional classified-activity notification may apply for ancillary warehousing.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOC emissions arise from trading and storage. Sanitary discharges must comply with municipal wastewater regulations. Dust and granule handling must meet occupational exposure limits for polymer dust under the Grand-Ducal Regulation on workplace health and safety, and measures must prevent dust explosion hazards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) for any warehouse premises; structural load verification from the municipal building authority; workplace safety inspection by the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) before employee occupancy.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg Inland Revenue (Administration des contributions directes, 'ACD') for direct taxes; Luxembourg Registration Duties, Estates and VAT Authority (Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA, 'AEDT') for VAT and indirect taxes; Customs and Excise Agency (Administration des douanes et accises) for customs and EORI numbers. National official portals: MyGuichet.lu and guichet.public.lu; VAT e-filing is performed through the AEDT's electronic VAT declaration service accessible via MyGuichet.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: A Luxembourg civil-law notary authenticates the SCSp constitutive deed and partnership agreement (no statutory minimum capital applies to an SCSp). Step 2: File the incorporation dossier with the Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, 'RCS') through the LBR e-Desk within one month of notarization; RCS registration is mandatory for a commercially active partnership and automatically transmits the entity data to the ACD. Step 3: The ACD issues the national identification number (13-digit 'matricule') and opens the direct tax account. Step 4: File the VAT commencement declaration (formulaire 010) with the AEDT within 15 days of commencing taxable economic activity; the AEDT assigns the Luxembourg VAT ID (format LU + 8 digits). An EU-established foreign entity may register directly; a non-EU/EEA-established entity must appoint an AEDT-approved VAT fiscal representative, who is jointly and severally liable for the entity's VAT. Step 5: Obtain an EORI number (LU + 8/9 digits) from the Customs and Excise Agency before the first import or export. Step 6: Where material, apply for an advance tax ruling from the ACD to confirm the pass-through classification, economic substance, and transfer pricing arrangements.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg applies statutory-form classification rather than a US-style check-the-box election. The SCSp is a contractual partnership without legal personality: it is fiscally transparent for corporate income tax and net wealth tax, with each partner taxed pro-rata on the allocable profit regardless of distribution, but it is directly subject to municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) at the partnership level where the enterprise is commercial; wholesale distribution of petrochemical polymers is a commercial activity, making RCS registration the operative choice of regime. For VAT, the SCSp is a taxable person in its own right. Available elective mechanisms include: (i) free drafting of profit and loss allocation ratios and capital structure in the partnership agreement, with no withholding tax on distributions to partners; (ii) VAT grouping ('assujetti unique') election under Article 62 of the VAT Law for Luxembourg group members; (iii) ACD advance tax rulings and advance pricing agreements confirming transparency, substance, financing, and transfer pricing; (iv) ATAD and ATAD II hybrid-mismatch documentation and disclosure filings to prevent double non-taxation arising from the SCSp's transparent status and foreign-law entity mismatches; (v) elections regarding input VAT recovery under partial-exemption regimes where mixed-use activities exist; and (vi) business transfer and exit neutrality elections under the Luxembourg VAT regime. No tax-exempt-zone election is available for trading income.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, 'TVA') - EU-harmonised VAT under Council Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Small-enterprise exemption under Article 64 of the Luxembourg VAT Law: annual turnover (excluding VAT) not exceeding EUR 35,000 qualifies for exemption; VAT registration is mandatory as soon as Luxembourg taxable turnover exceeds EUR 35,000, or when the SCSp makes taxable B2B supplies, performs intra-EU acquisitions subject to VAT, or imports goods. Non-established suppliers making supplies of goods in Luxembourg are required to register directly (EU-established businesses) or via a fiscal representative (non-EU-established businesses), irrespective of the turnover threshold, where the applicable B2B or consignment-stock routing rules so provide.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, fiscal stamping, or continuous transaction control (CTC) system is in force for domestic B2B invoices in Luxembourg during the current tax year. Electronic invoicing is voluntary in B2B; every invoice, whether paper or digital, must preserve authenticity of origin, integrity of content, and legibility pursuant to Article 68 of the VAT Law, with audit-proof archiving for 10 years. Mandatory e-invoicing applies only to B2G invoices to Luxembourg public authorities, which must be submitted in PEPPOL BIS Billing 3.0 format through a certified PEPPOL access point under the public procurement legislation. VAT returns are filed electronically on a monthly or quarterly basis through the AEDT e-declaration service. Under the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) reform, mandatory digital reporting and e-invoicing for cross-border B2B supplies will take effect from 1 July 2030; Luxembourg has not yet activated a domestic B2B e-invoicing mandate, but the SCSp's ERP and invoicing architecture should be ViDA-ready.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% VAT with recovery of input tax) applies under Article 52 of the Luxembourg VAT Law (implementing Article 146 of Directive 2006/112/EC) for exports of bulk virgin polyethylene and polypropylene granules supplied by the SCSp to non-EU buyers, provided: (i) the goods leave EU customs territory within 3 months (90 days) of the supply date; (ii) the export is evidenced by a customs export declaration cleared by the competent export office; (iii) transport documents (bill of lading, CMR, or air waybill) are consistent with the invoice, Incoterms, and payment flows; (iv) the buyer is situated outside the EU and does not divert the goods back into the EU; and (v) the SCSp's accounting records permit verifiable tracing from order to export to remittance. Intra-Community supplies to EU/EEA business customers are zero-rated under Article 53 of the VAT Law subject to the customer's valid EU VAT ID, evidence of movement to the destination member state within 90 days, and timely EC Sales List filing. Ancillary transport and insurance services related to non-EU goods are zero-rated under the export-services rules, and offshore services to non-EU customers follow B2B reverse-charge location rules where the recipient is an established taxable person.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document - SAD/EX1) with export ratification or confirmation from the customs office of export
Bill of Lading (or CMR consignment note / air waybill) evidencing physical exit of the goods from EU territory
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 / accepted proof of receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency
Commercial invoice, packing list, and certificate of analysis or weight certificate for the polymer granules
Proof of title transfer and Incoterms evidence, including transport contract and freight forwarding confirmation
For intra-EU zero-rating: customer VAT ID validation printout and EC Sales List (recapitulative statement) acknowledgment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT audit unit subjects export zero-rating claims to document-and-flow scrutiny, cross-checking customs export declarations against transport documents, Incoterms, ERP trails, and bank and FX records. Where export substantiation is incomplete or inconsistent, the AEDT retrospectively reassesses the supply at the 17% standard rate with statutory default interest on the under-declared VAT (currently 0.6% per month of arrears), plus administrative fines under Articles 74-84 of the VAT Law, including up to EUR 10,000 per offence for defective records and up to 20% of the evaded tax for incorrect or incomplete declarations. Deliberate export fraud, including forged customs documents, fictitious consignments, carousel or missing-trader routing, and fabricated inward remittance certificates, constitutes criminal VAT fraud punishable under Articles 86 and 86ter of the VAT Law and the General Tax Law by fines and imprisonment, with custodial sentences of up to five years in aggravated or organised cases, confiscation of assets, and publication of the conviction; the reassessment period extends to 10 years in fraud cases. The AEDT may order seizure of funds and enforcement against the partners of the SCSp on a joint-and-several basis where the partnership's assets are insufficient. In practice, an export zero-rating claim failing the 180-day FX repatriation benchmark is presumptively challenged as a sham export.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) together with the European Central Bank (ECB) in the Eurosystem; the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) is the supervisory authority for credit institutions and payment institutions
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a eurozone member, and the euro is fully convertible on both current and capital account. There are no exchange control laws, no approval requirements for profit remittances, and no restrictions on payments or transfers for international transactions. Cross-border capital movements are governed by EU Treaty freedoms and the EU Anti-Money Laundering / sanctions framework. The only practical hurdles are banking documentation, beneficial ownership transparency, and compliance with EU restrictive measures; these do not constitute convertibility or repatriation restrictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory obligation to surrender, convert, or repatriate export proceeds within a fixed timeline. Exporters may freely hold and manage foreign currency receivables in euro or other currencies. Resident enterprises are required solely to report direct investment flows and external positions to the BCL for balance-of-payments statistical purposes when the relevant legal threshold (generally EUR 12.5 million per transaction or annual aggregate) is triggered.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État, Luxembourg (BCEE)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account / Commercial LC Account
Operational Account / Capital Escrow Account / Commercial LC Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium – subject to critical constraints. A Luxembourg-licensed or EU-passported electronic money institution (EMI) under PSD2 may provide payment accounts, remittance services, FX conversion, and IBAN issuance for the SCSp. However, most non-bank EMIs do not have the capacity to issue irrevocable commercial letters of credit, receive large capital subscriptions, or handle trade finance documentation; therefore their use is feasible only as a secondary operational treasury rail. Offshore (non-EEA) digital EMIs generally cannot hold euro accounts on behalf of Luxembourg entities or access SEPA/TARGET2 clearing without a Luxembourg or EU branch or license, and are not considered acceptable primary banking infrastructure by Luxembourg counterparties or the CSSF.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg law does not impose a strict statutory mandate for physical attendance at a bank branch. In practice, Tier-1 banks accept remote onboarding using secure video identification and digital signatures, but nearly all require at least one senior manager or ultimate beneficial owner to complete a recorded interactive interview, and certain banks may require the general partner (manager) of the SCSp to be physically present before authorizing trade finance or high-risk clearing facilities. Pure remote account opening without any human control is rare and generally limited to low-volume payment accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex multi-jurisdictional ownership chain with interposed holding companies or intermediate partnerships
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled SCSp partnership agreement; full ownership diagram from ultimate beneficial owner down to the SCSp; corporate registers of each intermediate entity; legal opinion from Luxembourg counsel confirming tax transparency and substance; and a written source-of-wealth statement signed by the UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value petrochemical trading flows with unexpectedly high turnover relative to stated capital
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master purchase and sales agreements for polyethylene/polypropylene granules; pipeline of invoices, bills of lading, and warehouse receipts; internal risk and compliance framework; detailed 12-month cash flow forecast; and a letter from a reputable trade partner confirming commercial reality.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Counterparty-name screening or jurisdiction rating indicates exposure to sanctioned or embargoed commodities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive transaction-level sanctions screening report (EU, OFAC, UN); certificate of origin and end-user attestation for each shipment; compliance policy prohibiting trade with restricted entities; and engagement letter with an external compliance consultant acceptable to the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital contribution sourced from a non-EU trust, family foundation, or a jurisdiction not recognised by the bank
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full trust deed or foundation charter and certificates of registration; identification of settlor, protection committee, and beneficiaries; independent legal opinion regarding the source and transferability of capital; bank statement evidencing the trail from the origin fund; and official confirmation that the structure does not constitute a high-risk tax arrangement.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions from non-resident limited partners are routed via SWIFT MT103 or, for euro payments, via SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) / TARGET2. The payment must reference the exact legal name and registration number of the SCSp and identify the nature of the transaction as an equity contribution on the general ledger. For direct investment reporting to the BCL, the transaction must be flagged under the appropriate balance-of-payments classification. Funds are typically deposited into a dedicated capital escrow account in the SCSp's name and, upon admission of the limited partner, transferred to the main operational account. There are no foreign exchange surrender or licensing requirements for these capital installments.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements comprise: (1) SWIFT MT103/MT202 for high-value wire transfers to counterparties and refiners; (2) irrevocable commercial letters of credit evidenced by SWIFT MT700 issuance and MT707 amendments, issued by the Luxembourg account bank or a confirming correspondent, to guarantee payment against presentation of compliant shipping and quality documents; (3) documentary sight/demand guarantees under URDG 758 for tender and performance obligations; and (4) SEPA instant credit transfers for low-value euro disbursements within the EEA. Multi-currency trade settlements may be cleared over the correspondent network of the account bank or through a nostro account, subject to FX execution and liquidity fees.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX swaps (spot and forward legs) for short-term liquidity management
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (for term-matched financing structures)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for blocked or non-convertible exotic currencies where a deliverable local market does not exist; not applicable to EUR/USD
Plain vanilla FX options (e.g., EUR/USD calls and puts) for cap and floor strategies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of RCS registered particulars (Confirmation annuelle)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one calendar month following each anniversary of the entity's initial RCS registration; filing is accepted from 30 days before the anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine for late submission; repeated failure after formal notices may lead to automatic removal and judicial strike-off (radiation d'office) from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial owner register confirmation (Confirmation annuelle des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one calendar month following each anniversary of the initial RBE declaration; the annual confirmation must also cover any transfer of limited-partnership interests during the preceding year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 125,000 for non-confirmation or incomplete data; wilful false statements carry criminal penalties; repeated non-compliance may trigger RCS strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing with the RCS (only if the SCSp is not exempt under Article 74 of the Law of 10 August 1915)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - RCS (electronic filing platform)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of approval by the partners and, in any event, not later than seven months after the financial year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Commercial court fines for late filing or non-filing; persistent default may lead to compulsory winding-up proceedings or administrative strike-off after due notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Luxembourg direct tax return for the SCSp (income tax and municipal business tax allocation; Form 1001 with partnership annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD), Bureau d'imposition des sociétés
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year accounting period, on or before 30 June of the following year; extension to 31 December is available on request; for non-calendar year-end, due at the end of the sixth month after the financial year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge and procedural fine (up to EUR 5,000 in cases of tax adjustment), plus late-payment interest at 0.8% per month; for wilful non-filing, criminal tax sanctions may apply.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Luxembourg SCSp must appoint an independent approved statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises) if it exceeds two of the three thresholds under Article 76 of the Law of 10 August 1915: balance sheet total > EUR 4.4 million; net turnover > EUR 8.8 million; average employees > 50. An audit is also compulsory if the SCSp has issued securities admitted to trading on an EU regulated market or if the partnership agreement or a shareholder request so requires.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: LUX GAAP under the Law of 10 August 1915 as amended and the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 10 April 2017; IFRS as adopted by the EU may be used for voluntary consolidated financial statements; accounts are prepared in euros.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must file and annually confirm its beneficial ownership data with the RBE. Confirmation is due before each RBE anniversary and must identify every natural person with direct or indirect beneficial ownership of more than 25% of the partnership interests or control rights. Any transfer of limited-partnership interests that changes UBO data must be reported to the RBE within 30 days of the change; the annual RBE confirmation is a separate filing even if performed in the same calendar period as the RCS annual confirmation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of members / limited partners (register des associés commanditaires)
Register of general partner and managers (register des associés commandités et gérants)
Statutory minute book of partner and general-partner resolutions
Register of transfers of partnership interests (if interests are registered in nominal form)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,500 - 16,500 (approximately EUR 5,000 - 15,000) for a mandatory audit of a small to mid-sized SCSp; no audit fee is incurred when the SCSp is below the statutory audit thresholds and no audit is otherwise required.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: As a fiscally transparent entity (Société en Commandite Spéciale), the SCSp is not subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax (CIT), municipal business tax (MBT), or net wealth tax (NWT) at the entity level. Each partner is taxed personally in their respective jurisdiction of residence or permanent establishment. This pass-through designation is statutorily available without specific government approval, provided the SCSp lacks corporate status. No statutory tax holiday is applicable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No separate Luxembourg tax return is filing for the SCSp itself. However, the SCSp must file an annual information return (Déclaration pour l’inscription au registre des bénéficiaires effectifs and the RBE beneficial ownership filing) and, when it has Luxembourg-source income allocated to a Luxembourg-resident partner, that partner files Form 100 (CIT) or Form 1000 (for individuals) through the MyGuichet.lu electronic portal. Additionally, the SCSp must file an annual statistical return (modèle 25/03) if it holds qualifying assets or performs activities subject to the Central Balance Sheet Office (CSSF).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Corporate tax return (Form 100/1000): no later than six months following the end of the relevant fiscal year (i.e., by 31 December for a calendar-year taxpayer, unless an extension is granted). The RBE beneficial ownership declaration must be filed annually and no later than one month after any change. The statistical return must be filed within five months after the balance sheet date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity name, legal form (SCSp), registered address, registration number (RCS Luxembourg), and statutory representative details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident partner, the SCSp’s local agent or the partner’s Luxembourg tax representative must ensure Box 0 identifies the partner’s name, foreign tax ID, and permanent address. The SCSp’s own RCS number must be referenced in any communication.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation and disclosure of the contractual profit-sharing percentages and capital contributions for each partner, as set out in the partnership agreement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must list their profit share ratio and the corresponding amount of Luxembourg-source income (if any) attributed to a Luxembourg permanent establishment. Passive foreign partners (no PE) enter “0” in Luxembourg-source income boxes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross wholesale trading revenue derived from sales of virgin polyethylene and polypropylene granules, including invoicing under SWIFT LC and irrevocable LC payment rails.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident partner not carrying on a Luxembourg trade through a permanent establishment reports only sales attributable to a Luxembourg PE. Pure offshore principal trading without a PE is excluded from Luxembourg taxable turnover.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold (COGS), freight, handling, insurance, storage, bank charges, and allocable overheads. Transfer pricing adjustments and arm’s length documentation must corroborate cross-border margins.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must ensure expenses deducted against Luxembourg-source income are directly connected to the PE activity. Head-office overhead allocations must satisfy the OECD Authorised OECD Approach and Luxembourg administrative practice.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the assimilated corporate taxable base for each partner subject to Luxembourg tax. For a resident corporate partner, headline rates apply: CIT 17% plus 7% solidarity surcharge plus municipal business tax (variable, max 10.5%), aggregate 24.94% for Luxembourg City.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident corporate partners without a PE, Box 4 should be nil. If the partner is resident in a DTA country, treaty tie-breaker and business profits (Article 7) rules apply; the SCSp itself never files a standalone corporate return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 / Withholding Tax Credits and Prepayments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reporting of any Luxembourg withholding taxes on dividends, interest, or royalties derived by the SCSp, and any tax prepayments (acomptes) made by or on behalf of partners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must attach Form 6 (income tax claim) or a refund request to the Luxembourg tax office (Administration des contributions directes) supported by Form A declarations and source-country certificates if treaty relief is claimed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual RBE declaration: fines up to EUR 1,250 per offence and publication of a court order. Late statistical return filing: penalties up to EUR 2,000 per month, with a maximum of EUR 20,000. For a Luxembourg-resident taxable partner, late CIT return (Form 100): surcharge of 10% of the net tax due, daily interest at 0.6% per month (annual effective 7.2%), plus increased assessment if the return is filed after a formal reminder. Non-resident partners with a Luxembourg PE face the same surcharge regime. Criminal penalties for failure to file tax returns can reach EUR 25,000 and imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% under Luxembourg domestic law when distributions are made by a qualifying Luxembourg company to a non-resident corporate partner. However, due to the pass-through nature of the SCSp, distributions to partners are not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax as dividends, provided the SCSp is not treated as a corporation under Luxembourg law. Luxembourg no longer levies a source-state withholding on partnership profit allocations.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Where any residual Luxembourg withholding tax applies (e.g., if the SCSp is reclassified under domestic anti-abuse rules or when the partnership is treated as a corporation by a treaty partner), the non-resident partner must: (i) obtain a Luxembourg Certificate of Tax Residence (Formulaire 167) from the Administration des contributions directes; (ii) submit the DTA relief application (Formulaire 300 / 300A) through the Luxembourg tax collector (Recette) before the payment date or, if not possible, within three months after the end of the calendar year; (iii) attach an approved Power of Attorney and a statement of the ultimate beneficial owner; (iv) rely on the Multilateral Instrument (MLI) and the OEEC 2017 Model provisions. A reduced rate or full exemption under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive (when applicable, for EU corporate shareholders holding at least 10% for 12 months) can be invoked administratively without prior approval.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic law in principle exempts interest and royalties paid by a Luxembourg payer from source withholding tax. Statutory fallback rates under treaties: 15% for royalties and 15% for interest (subject to beneficial ownership and absence of abusive arrangement). For associated enterprises, the arm’s length principle applies under Article 9 of the OECD Model; Luxembourg applies a 0% withholding on interest and royalties to most EU counterparts under the Interest and Royalty Directive (2003/49/EC) if 25% direct ownership is met and the beneficial owner is established in an EU state.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The SCSp, as a special limited partnership, is generally not captured by the OECD Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) unless it performs relevant activity. However, Luxembourg administrative practice and the ATAD implementation require adequate substance for treaty benefits. For a wholesale trading SCSp, substance is evidenced by: business premises in Luxembourg, full-time personnel with autonomous decision-making on pricing and contracting, physical inventory risk if the partner claims PE status, and board/director minutes evidencing control over risk. The Grand-Ducal Regulation of 21 June 2019 (permanent establishment and import of partnership assets) further requires that any Luxembourg PE of a foreign partner maintains accounting records, a dedicated bank account, and operational autonomy.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately allocating all trading profits to a non-resident partner in a tax haven without performing any actual business activity in that jurisdiction, while conducting real procurement and resale decisions in Luxembourg through the SCSp’s managers or employees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 120 of the Luxembourg General Tax Law (Abgabenordnung), tax evasion triggers criminal fines up to EUR 100,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years (Article 399 of the Criminal Code). Additionally, a 50% civil penalty on the understated tax is imposed, plus late payment interest of 7.2% per annum. The taxpayer bears the burden of rebutting the presumption of taxable presence in Luxembourg.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director/manager of an SCSp who knowingly submits false tax declarations is personally liable for the full amount of unpaid taxes and penalties (joint and several liability under Article 1645 of the General Tax Law). The Director may face criminal conviction and travel bans; the court can order seizure of personal assets and restriction of cross-border movement if the unpaid tax exceeds EUR 100,000.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SCSp with no employees, no premises, no bank account, and no transactional records while claiming treaty benefits or pass-through status for large-scale bulk petrochemical trading profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Luxembourg tax authorities may apply the substance-over-form doctrine and reclassify the SCSp as a fully taxable corporate entity (in which case the headline corporate regime applies). This triggers back-taxes, 50% negligence penalties, and potential denial treaty relief. The entity may also be struck from the Luxembourg Business Registers if it has no economic activity for three consecutive years, leading to dissolution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors cannot rely on limited liability when the partnership is reclassified as a corporate dummy. Courts may pierce the veil and hold directors personally liable for all corporate taxes, penalties, and third-party trade debts. In severe cases, a ban of up to 5 years from serving as a director in Luxembourg is imposed, and the director’s own travel documents may be withheld pending payment of tax liabilities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file accurate beneficial ownership information with the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) or concealing the ultimate beneficial owner behind unverified corporate layers, particularly when SWIFT LC payment rails are used.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to EUR 250,000 for legal entities and EUR 250,000 for individuals (new Law of 13 January 2019). The Luxembourg Business Registers can publish non-compliance and suspend the entity's rights, including entitlement to tax treaty benefits. Additionally, criminal AML sanctions can reach 5 years’ imprisonment if money laundering is proven (Law of 12 November 2004).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of an SCSp are personally liable for AML penalties if they knowingly or negligently fail to identify the need to file the RBE declaration. They may be subject to imprisonment up to 6 months for mere non-filing of RBE data. The court may impose a travel ban and order the winding-up of the entity, with the director forced to compensate all third parties for losses arising from the absence of transparency.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Buying virgin petrochemical granules from an offshore affiliate at an artificially inflated price and reselling them through Luxembourg at a lower price, shifting profits outside Luxembourg, without complying with Chapter V of the OECD Guidelines or maintaining a local file.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Luxembourg primary adjustment (i.e., re-determination of taxable income) plus a secondary adjustment applied as a deemed distribution or capital contribution. A penalty of up to 200% of the understated tax can be levied if the taxpayer has not performed a correct transfer pricing study. Interest accrues at 7.2% per annum. The General Tax Law enables the tax authority to approximate profit margins using a default net margin of 5%-10% for wholesale trading if records are absent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or execute a non-arm’s length transaction in breach of their fiduciary duties are personally liable for the resulting tax deficit under Luxembourg civil law (joint and several with the partnership). In criminal cases, the director may be sentenced to imprisonment of up to 3 years and a fine of EUR 15,000 for false accounting (Article 119 of the Criminal Code).
